Energy and momentum are $E=\hbar c\omega$ in joules and $\mathbf p=\hbar\mathbf k$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$.

Spinor tests with compact spacelike-separated supports have vanishing anticommutators with one another and with each other's adjoints. Consequently, even polynomials in the bounded smeared fields commute across spacelike-separated regions.

The fermionic Fock space of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]] carries a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\widetilde G$ such that $$U(\tilde g)\Psi(F)U(\tilde g)^{-1}=\Psi(\tau_{\tilde g}F).$$

For every real $x$, $$\sin(x+\pi/2)=\cos x,\quad\cos(x+\pi/2)=-\sin x,\quad\sin(x+\pi)=-\sin x,\quad\cos(x+\pi)=-\cos x.$$ In particular, $$\sin(\pi/2)=1,\quad\cos(\pi/2)=0,\quad\sin\pi=0,\quad\cos\pi=-1.$$

derivations.claim: Under the adopted model, the conditional field proof establishes CAR, the tested Dirac equation and vanishing cross anticommutators for spacelike-separated supports. Taking adjoints supplies the adjoint-adjoint case; swapping each of r and s factors gives sign (-1)^(rs), equal to +1 when both degrees are even, and bilinearity gives finite even-polynomial commutation.

The covariance supplier constructs the strongly continuous unitary Fock lift and exact test pullback. The explicit rotation matrix and pi-shift theorem give S_R(2π)=-I_4; substituting x=π into the pi-shift identities gives cos(2π)=1 and sin(2π)=0, hence S_R(4π)=I_4. The test pullbacks are -F and F, and field antilinearity gives the field sign. The same supplier gives invariant vacuum, cyclic global field algebra, and the Fock 2π/4π actions.

The Fock translation generator is distinct from the first-quantized h_D: the supplier gives nonnegative particle and antiparticle translation energies, unique zero-energy vacuum and the μ>0 gap; since μ=m_rest,SI c/ħ, multiplying by ħc yields SI rest energy m_rest,SI c².
